extracted.intended_audience: AGU authors, journal editors, and the geoscience research community concerned with peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evidence-based policy for increasing demographic and geographic diversity among journal peer reviewers, aimed at changes to author submission forms and editorial selection practices across AGU journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage a balanced reviewer pool (gender, age, ethnicity, country)
rubrics_metrics.description: AGU is explicitly encouraging a more balanced pool of reviewers for journal manuscripts in terms of gender, age cohort, ethnicity, and country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames this as an explicit organizational objective based on data showing underrepresentation (especially of women, younger scientists, and researchers from Asia and Africa). This is the overarching desideratum that drives other measures described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should include diverse suggested reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Please help us improve the diversity of our reviewer pool by including women, young scientists, and members of other underrepresented groups in your suggested reviewers (e.g., age, ethnic, and international diversity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement was added to submission forms (tested on GRL) and is intended both to guide authors when they supply suggested reviewers and to prompt more diverse suggestions; the experiment showed a significant increase in the percentage of female reviewers suggested after adding this note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include reminder statement across journals and to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: The reminder statement about including women, young scientists, and other underrepresented groups will be included not only in the instructions for authors but also as a reminder to the editors when they select reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rollout across all AGU journals — place the text in submission instructions and present it to editors during reviewer selection to influence both author suggestions and editorial choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand diversity among editorial leadership and boards
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors in chief have worked to expand diversity on their teams (both editors and associate editors) and to discuss the larger bias among peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improving reviewer diversity should be complemented by diversifying editorial teams so selection practices and priorities better reflect a range of perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit more younger scientists and more researchers from underrepresented regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Data clearly show that AGU needs to engage more younger scientists in reviewing and also more scientists from Asia and Africa; AGU currently recruits a large proportion of reviewers from the United States, Canada, and Europe whereas accepted authors reside roughly equally in North America, Europe, and Asia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target recruitment efforts (e.g., editor outreach, conferences, institutional visits) toward younger cohorts and underrepresented regions to better match the geographic distribution of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely uncritically on author-suggested reviewer lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias initiated from author suggestions and persisted through invitations from editors; author-suggested lists contributed to underuse of women as reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should be aware that author-provided reviewer suggestions may systematically underrepresent certain groups and should actively compensate for that bias when selecting reviewers (for example, by explicitly seeking women and international reviewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide training: workshops and webinars on reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: AGU editors have been conducting workshops on reviewing internationally and AGU Publications has conducted webinars on reviewing, including 'How to Write Effective Reviews (and Improve Your Own Manuscript)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in reviewer training and outreach (workshops at conferences, webinars, visits to institutions) to broaden the pool of qualified reviewers and improve willingness/ability to accept review invitations across regions and age cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and publicly report reviewer-diversity data
rubrics_metrics.description: AGU will continue to collect and report data on reviewer diversity in its scientific publishing and provide regular updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing measurement and transparency are required to track progress, identify persistent gaps (e.g., geographic or age-related), and inform further interventions; the article uses matched membership/editorial data and accounts for age in its analysis.
